config.title: Databases & consistency

intro.title: Databases & consistency
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple simulation of a social media post system to understand how databases handle data consistency. You will learn the core concept of eventual consistency by modeling a scenario where a post's like count updates across multiple servers. The main technologies involved are basic JavaScript objects to represent database records and functions to simulate read/write operations. This hands-on approach will help you grasp why consistency matters in distributed systems and how different consistency models affect user experience.
intro.usecase: Database consistency patterns are critical in any system where data is read and written by multiple users or services, such as e-commerce platforms, banking applications, and social media feeds. For example, when you update your profile picture on a social network, the change must instantly reflect across your profile, comments, and friend lists without showing outdated images—this requires strong consistency. In an online shopping cart, ensuring that inventory counts decrement accurately when an item is purchased, preventing overselling, relies on consistency models. Developers implement these patterns to build reliable features like real-time collaborative editors, financial transaction ledgers, and user notification systems where data integrity is non-negotiable.

objectives: Implement a basic database schema to model a simple data domain
Apply CRUD operations to manipulate records within a database
Configure a database connection and initialize a data store
Construct queries to retrieve and filter data based on specific criteria
Integrate a database with a simple application to persist state
Manipulate data consistency by implementing basic transaction logic
Update database records while maintaining referential integrity
